edges.description: Mutant HP1-beta localizes throughout the nucleus without accumulation at chromocenters despite wild-type HP1-beta being present, demonstrating the dominant-negative effect in primary neurons.
edges.limitations: The behavioral battery was largely normal apart from latency-to-peak startle; the model captures the molecular/cellular dominant-negative defect rather than the human cognitive phenotype, and only chromodomain missense alleles were modeled.

edges.description: Mutant mice show increased latency-to-peak acoustic startle response, interpreted as delayed neurotransmission; overt brain structure and most behaviors are normal.
edges.limitations: Mouse behavior does not reproduce the human developmental delay, intellectual disability, or autistic phenotype; the only robust deficit is the latency-to-peak startle response.

evidence.snippet: This syndrome is caused by heterozygous missense variants in CBX1, which encodes heterochromatin protein 1 beta (HP1β). These variants are situated within the chromodomain of HP1β

nodes.description: De novo missense variants in CBX1 substitute conserved residues (Thr51, Trp52, Asn57, Leu40, Cys60) within the HP1-beta chromodomain, the domain that reads methylated histone H3K9. The variants reduce HP1-beta binding to H3K9me2/3 and mislocalize HP1-beta away from heterochromatic chromocenters to a homogeneous nuclear distribution.
